items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Frank Holstein is mentioned by the interviewer as the source of a claim about the Blue Note, and later appears in the interviewee's narrative as a staff member at the club who turned off the microphone and directed George Brunis, but no direct personal interaction or relationship between Art Hodes a

ctx.x: Yeah. And the next time around, you don't have to worry, we'll kill them. They'll take us, anyway. That's the -- now I got to tell Freddie Moore he's through.
That's what eventually killed the Blue Note, according to Frank Holstein. If you wanted Duke, you had to take Joe Blow.

What it did to me was, I got zutty. Now, last time I worked with zutty was on Decca Records. And zutty and I were very together. But now, here I'm not drinking, I'm not smoking, I'm not -- very straight kick. And probably not playing as good, because it takes a while to start -- if you've been playing high and drunk all the time, you get sober, not drink and not get high, it's going to take you a while to find your way around. And that I have to admit, I can't fault nobody.
